title: Logarithmic differentials of a strict morphism as a pushout
statement:
Let $(Z,L)\xrightarrow{c}(W,M)\xrightarrow{g}(S,N)$ be morphisms of fine log schemes on arbitrary schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Fine log structures mean sheaves of commutative monoids on the small etale site, with a structural map $\alpha$ to the multiplicative structure ring sheaf inducing an isomorphism from the inverse image of the units onto the units, and admitting etale-local charts by finitely generated integral monoids, with associated logification as in [lem-per-integral-chart-logification-thickening]. Assume $c$ is strict: $L$ is the log structure associated to $c^{-1}M\to\mathcal O_Z$. No smoothness, flatness, finite-presentation or Noetherian assumption is made.

For a morphism $v:(U,H)\to(V,F)$, define $\omega_v$ on the small etale site as the sheaf of $\mathcal O_U$-modules generated by $da$ for functions and $d\log h$ for log sections, modulo additivity and the Leibniz rule for $d$, $d\log(hh')=d\log h+d\log h'$, $d\alpha(h)=\alpha(h)d\log h$, and $da=d\log h=0$ for functions and log sections pulled back from the base.
Use ordinary relative differential sheaves [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], regarded on small etale sites via [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module], and put $c^*E=\mathcal O_Z\otimes_{c^{-1}\mathcal O_W}c^{-1}E$ using sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Set $A=c^*\Omega^1_{W/S}$, $B=\Omega^1_{Z/S}$ and $C=c^*\omega_g$. Let $u:A\to B$ send $1\otimes da$ to $d(c^\sharp a)$, and let $v:A\to C$ send $1\otimes da$ to $1\otimes da$ with the latter $da$ interpreted as a logarithmic differential. Define
$$P=(B\oplus C)/\operatorname{im}\bigl(A\xrightarrow{(u,-v)}B\oplus C\bigr),$$
where image and quotient are taken in sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The canonical morphism
$$\Phi:P\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{gc},\qquad [(b,e)]\longmapsto j(b)+\iota(e)$$
is an isomorphism, where $j(da)=da$, $\iota(1\otimes da)=d(c^\sharp a)$ and $\iota(1\otimes d\log m)=d\log(c^\flat m)$. Equivalently the square with upper row $A\xrightarrow{u}B$, lower row $C\xrightarrow{\iota}\omega_{gc}$ and vertical maps $v,j$ is a pushout of $\mathcal O_Z$-module sheaves. Its inverse on local symbols is
$$da\longmapsto[(da,0)],\qquad d\log(c^\flat m)\longmapsto[(0,1\otimes d\log m)],\qquad d\log t\longmapsto[(t^{-1}dt,0)]\quad(t\in\mathcal O_Z^\times).$$
These formulas agree whenever a local log section has different expressions in the associated log structure, and commute with restriction.

source.place: Agent refinement of the strict-log differential pushout proof.

proof.text: Let d=u followed by coprod.inl minus v followed by coprod.inr. Its cokernel P and the two quotient inclusions are a pushout: cokernel.condition gives commutativity; cokernel.desc applied to coprod.desc gives every cocone map; cokernel.π is epi and coprod.hom_ext gives uniqueness. This is the proved private lemma quotient_pushout.

source.place: Original pushout Step 9, proved categorically in Lean.

proof.text: Descend the canonical cocone (j,iota) through P to get φ. Apply [lem-per-strict-log-symbol-extension] with T=P, p=qB, q=qC to obtain ψ and all three inverse formulas.

The composite j followed by ψ equals qB by the ordinary presentation universal property. The composite iota followed by ψ equals qC by the C-generator extensionality: on ordinary generators use the quotient relation evaluated on 1 tensor da and the u,v normalizations; on log generators use the extension formula. Consequently φ followed by ψ is the identity by pushout hom_ext.

source.place: Original pushout Step 8, proved in Lean.

proof.text: Apply the uniqueness clause of [lem-per-strict-log-symbol-extension] to T=ω_gc and the canonical cocone (j,iota). The identity map satisfies its two symbol formulas by normalization. The composite ψ followed by φ satisfies the same formulas by the quotient descent identities. Uniqueness makes ψ followed by φ the identity.

source.place: Original pushout Step 8, proved in Lean.

proof.text: Use φ and ψ with the two proved inverse identities as the isomorphism Φ. Transport the cokernel pushout square through Φ, and retain the extension formulas for Φ inverse. This gives the exact original theorem with every displayed normalization.

The item is still unsplit on live and side-live, so no other group has superseded it. proof_deps equals the union of uses. Steps 1-2 build the associated log structure from scratch on an arbitrary scheme: Q = H x O^x modulo the congruence generated by (he,t)~(h,beta(e)t), then CMon sheafification. The unit axiom holds because a section with unit image is locally [1,beta(h)t]. The universal property holds because f(e)=j_K(beta(e)). Step 3 is well defined because j u = iota v = d(c^sharp a), and the structural relation is preserved since c^sharp alpha_M = alpha_L c^flat. Step 4 gives D(beta h) = beta(h) l(h) from q_B u = q_C v. Steps 5-7: l(e) = lambda(beta e) respects the congruence, the relation D(beta(h)t) = alpha_L(l) l_L(l) checks out, and N maps to 0. Steps 8-9: both composites are the identity on local generators, and the pushout is the cokernel universal property. Small cases agree: c=id, trivial log structures, the log point Spec k -> Spec k[x] (P = k dlog x), and the empty scheme. The nearby nodes (trf-associated-log-universal-stalks, per/sfb chart-logification-thickening, per-prelog-chart-fs-universal, the log-differential calculus nodes) are Noetherian, use a global chart or assume log smoothness, so none is a duplicate.
